Among them, line segment CM together with side CD and side DM encloses the upper-left triangle DCM, which is one of the three equal-area regions. According to the problem, the side length of the square is 3 cm, so the area of the square is 3×3=9 cm^2. The three parts have equal areas, so the area of each part is 9÷3=3 cm^2. The base DC of triangle DCM is one side of the square, DC=3 cm; DM is on side AD and is perpendicular to DC, so the area of triangle DCM is (1/2)×DC×DM=(1/2)×3×DM. raw_record.question_text: Square $ABCD$ has sides of length $3\mathrm{~cm}$. The points $M$ and $N$ lie on $AD$ and $AB$ so that $CM$ and $CN$ split the square into three pieces of the same area. What is the length of $DM$?

method.method_draft: Use the top-left triangular piece directly. From the image, identify that segment CM and the sides CD and DM enclose triangle DCM, which is one of the three equal-area pieces. From the text, the square has side length 3 cm, so its area is 9 cm^2 and each piece has area 3 cm^2. Since DC is a side of the square, DC = 3, and DM is perpendicular to DC. Apply the triangle area formula: area(DCM) = (1/2)(DC)(DM) = (1/2)(3)(DM). Set this equal to 3 and solve DM = 2 cm.
method.CoT_raw: 图像显示正方形ABCD中，D在左上，C在右上，A在左下，B在右下；M在边AD上，N在边AB上；线段CM和CN从顶点C出发，把正方形分成三块。其中，线段CM与边CD、边DM围成左上方的三角形DCM，这就是三块等面积区域中的一块。根据题意，正方形边长为3 cm，所以正方形面积为3×3=9 cm^2。三块面积相等，因此每块面积为9÷3=3 cm^2。三角形DCM的底边DC是正方形的一条边，DC=3 cm；DM在边AD上，与DC垂直，所以三角形DCM面积为(1/2)×DC×DM=(1/2)×3×DM。令其等于3，得到(3/2)DM=3，所以DM=2 cm。

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and the other regions rather than the top triangle directly. From the image, set coordinates A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(3,3), D=(0,3), with M=(0,m) on AD and N=(n,0) on AB. From the text, each of the three pieces has area 9/3 = 3 cm^2. First use the right triangular piece CBN: its base BN = 3-n and height CB = 3, so (1/2)(3)(3-n)=3, giving n=1. Then use the middle quadrilateral AMCN. By the shoelace formula, area(AMCN) = (3m+3n)/2. Substitute n=1 and set the area equal to 3: (3m+3)/2=3, so m=1. Since AD=3 and AM=m=1, DM=3-1=2 cm.

Reasoning: Set coordinates as A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(3,3), and D=(0,3). Let M=(0,m) on AD and N=(n,0) on AB. The square has area 3×3=9, so each of the three equal-area pieces has area 9/3=3 cm^2. Consider triangle CBN. Its base is BN=3−n and its height is CB=3, so its area is (1/2)(3)(3−n). Setting this equal to 3 gives (3/2)(3−n)=3, so 3−n=2 and n=1. Now consider quadrilateral AMCN. Using the shoelace formula on A=(0,0), M=(0,m), C=(3,3), N=(1,0), its area is (3m+3n)/2. Since n=1, this becomes (3m+3)/2. Set it equal to 3: (3m+3)/2=3, so 3m+3=6, hence m=1. Therefore AM=1 cm. Since AD=3 cm, DM=3−1=2 cm.
